title: Polaroid I-2 - Physical Camera Dials & Instant Photo Frame

affordance_translation.physical_behavior: An instant camera's top-plate control dials (aperture, shutter, mode rings) with tactile detents; instant film ejecting from the slot; the white-framed square photo as the product's own output.
affordance_translation.digital_mechanic: 3D camera model anchors the layout; a 'camera setting explore tool' lets users rotate real dials to learn I-2 features before purchase; scroll drives the camera through exploded/assembly states; photo gallery items render as freshly ejected instant photos with white polaroid frames.

design_tokens.borders: Nearly borderless; instant-photo white frames (~10-12%) are the only hard edges; dial knurling rendered as fine radial ridges in 3D
design_tokens.elevation: Photographic depth from 3D lighting and shadows cast by the camera model; UI chrome itself flat
design_tokens.typography: Compact uppercase grotesque labels echoing engraved camera legends; minimal supporting serif/sans body

interactive_mechanics: Rotatable 3D camera dials as product-feature explorer (rotation = parameter change)
Homepage intro animation of film ejecting into the hero photo frame
Gallery photos presented as freshly developed instants
usability_notes: E-commerce with education: dial-explorer converts spec-sheet features into muscle memory, ideal for prosumer cameras. Two-color palette keeps photography dominant. Risks: 3D interactivity needs mobile fallbacks and clear rotate affordances; dial controls must not gate purchase paths. Awwwards SOTD 7.48; dev award animation 8.0.
